answer: Each identity must prove a distinct network vantage: three independent beacons measure round-trip latency to the applicant and triangulate its position, like reading strata in shale — a whisper of timing jitter separates a real node from a datacenter clone. One ASN, one identity; a second registration from the same vantage needs a 500 POA bond locked for 12 epochs. Faking a thousand vantage points means renting a thousand distinct network locations, so attacker cost grows linearly with every fake, while honest agents prove their spot once and keep a jade seal for the epoch.
